title.title: Clique-free graphs behave like triangle-free ones
title.subtitle: Claim: $K_r$-free graphs have independent sets of size $c_r\,n \log d / d$, and need $O(\Delta/\log\Delta)$ colours

plain: Forbid any tight-knit group of $r$ mutual friends, and a network must hold a large group of strangers

beats.text: Graphs with no $K_r$, $r \ge 4$, and average degree $d$: how big an independent set?
For 45 years every argument for $r \ge 4$ lost a $\log\log$ factor
The claim removes it, and colours such graphs with $O(\Delta/\log\Delta)$ colours

steps: Give vertices weights that maximise an entropy-like score
Splitting vertices along random walks shows triangles stay rare
With few triangles, a large independent set falls out

achievement.label: AEKS (1981) and Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov (1999) conjectures
achievement.context: Both for $K_r$-free graphs with $r \ge 4$; the triangle-free case was classical
achievement.note: Only the independence bound is in Lean; the colouring paper is unformalized

verify.detail: In Lean: the independence bound for $K_r$-free graphs. Not the colouring theorem
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: Forbid a clique. How big must the largest group of strangers be?
An entropy score keeps triangles rare, then a large stranger set falls out.
Claimed: the log log loss is gone.

sources.quote: Shearer, RSA 7 (1995) 269–271 gave Omega_r(n log d/(d log log d))
AEKS proved Omega_r(n log log d/d)
(a) is the Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov conjecture ('Coloring graphs with sparse neighborhoods', JCTB 77 (1999))
